data.name: Second
data.comment: The symbol for seconds, alone: shown after the Timing panel's box in Length mode, and the unit the box accepts when the user types it ("2 s"). Use the same symbol as in SecondsFormat. Keep it short and easy to type (the English "s" is always accepted too).

data.name: FramesPerSecond
data.comment: The abbreviation for frames per second, alone: shown after the Timing panel's box in Per second mode, and the unit the box accepts when the user types it ("30 fps"). Use the same abbreviation as in FramesPerSecondFormat. Keep it short and easy to type (the English "fps" is always accepted too).

data.name: SecondsFormat
data.comment: A number of seconds: a video length under a minute ("24.7 s"), a Length or Per photo preset ("30 s", "0.25 s"), the ends of the length bar ("0 s", "60 s"). {0} the number, already written with your decimal separator. Keep it as short as the English: five presets share a 280 px row.

data.name: MinutesSecondsFormat
data.comment: A video length from one minute to under an hour ("1 min 12 s"). {0} the whole minutes, {1} the whole seconds (0 to 59).

data.name: HoursMinutesFormat
data.comment: A video length from one hour ("1 h 02 min"). {0} the whole hours, {1} the minutes, always two digits ("02").

data.name: FramesPerSecondFormat
data.comment: A frame rate ("30 fps", "29.97 fps"). {0} the rate, already written with your decimal separator.

data.name: SecondsPerPhotoFormat
data.comment: How long each photo stays on screen ("2 s per photo", "0.5 s per photo"). {0} the seconds, already written with your decimal separator. Use the same words as TimingText.UnitSecondsPerPhoto.

data.name: DefaultName
data.comment: The name of a project that has no folder name to take: the window title and the file name the Save dialog suggests ("Timelapse.mp4"), so use no character a file name cannot have (\ / : * ? " < > |).
